newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ING BARINGS REVISES HUNGARIAN SHARE EPSS.
newsitem.headline: ING BARINGS REVISES HUNGARIAN SHARE EPSS.

text.p: In the October issue of its "Eastern European Monthly" ING Barings revised its earnings/share (EPS) forecasts for several Budapest-traded stocks and in some cases also revised its recommendations.
ING Barings revised its EPS estimate upwards for tile manufacturer Zalakeramia Rt to 523 forints from 449 forints for 1996 and its EPS forecast to 642 forints from 617 forints for 1997.

The securities house attributed the revision to the fact that 1996 results are positively affected by the sale of the company's treasury shares. It left its recommendation unchanged at "long-term buy."

ING raised its EPS estimate to 460 forints from 431 forints for 1996 but lowered its forecast to 583 forints from 589 forints for 1997 for gas distributor Primagaz , saying that "provisions are likely to be written back in IAS results."
The securities house revised Primagaz's recommendation to "buy" from "long-term buy."

ING Barings raised its EPS estimate to 687 forints from 630 forints for 1996 for chemical company Borsodchem . "(This is because) provisions are likely to be written back in IAS results and PVC prices have started to rise since mid-September," it said.
The brokerage forecasts Borsodchem's 1997 EPS at 810 forints. The stocks's recommendation was left unchanged at "long-term buy."
Plastics industrial Pannonplast 's EPS forecast was left steady at 390 forints for 1996 and at 439 forints for 1997, but the share's recommendation was revised downward to "long-term buy" from "buy."
"Although the stock is still attractive, the recent price rise has led us to downgrade our recommendation from buy to long-term buy," ING Barings said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Zalakeramia shares stood at 7,000 forints, up five at 0956 GMT, Pannonplast traded at 5,095 forints, up 45, at 1006 GMT.
Borsodchem, suspended on Monday, soared to a new high of 3,185 forints and at 1007 GMT it stood at 3,150 forints, up 165.
On Tuesday no deals have yet been concluded for Primagaz.
